Two caveats on precision:

So the granted portfolio (485) is far smaller than the filed count, and the FY25 filing surge has yet to convert into grants.

For context, this is separate from RIL's own O2C filings: RIL O2C filed 48 new patent applications and secured approval for 28 patents, with a total of 1,156 patents granted to RIL as of March 31, 2025.

The report does not give a year-by-year breakdown of Jio's prior filings, so it isn't possible to confirm from these documents whether FY25 was a genuine one-off spike or part of a multi-year ramp.

## Size of the facilities

Reliance's FY25 fund-raising disclosure describes two offshore facilities, the larger of which was a syndicated term loan package:

Reliance secured Syndicated Term Loan Facilities of approximately $3 billion equivalent, which the Company secured to refinance maturing debt obligations [RELIANCE-FY25#0029].

For context, this sat alongside a second offshore tranche: RIL tied up ~$1 billion equivalent green SACE Push facilities supported by the Italian Export Credit Agency (SACE) to finance capital expenditure towards eligible green projects — the first such fully green-labelled facility for the Company [RELIANCE-FY25#0029]. Together, the offshore programme was roughly $4 billion equivalent, raised as part of what the report calls a multi-currency, multi-instrument financing strategy whose proceeds were primarily used to fund green capital expenditures and refinance upcoming debt maturities [RELIANCE-FY25#0029].

## Conversion to rupees crore

At a current USD/INR mid-market rate of about ₹95.87, $3 billion works out to roughly **₹28,760 crore**. The $1 billion ECA tranche would be a further ~₹9,590 crore, putting the combined offshore raise near ₹38,350 crore at today's rate.

## Caveats on the conversion

- **The rate is today's, not the transaction rate.** The loans were syndicated during FY25, when the rupee traded materially stronger (broadly in the mid-80s per dollar). Converted at a rate nearer the time of drawdown, $3 billion would have been closer to ₹25,000–26,000 crore. So the ₹28,760 crore figure is a mark-to-today translation, not the rupee amount Reliance actually booked.
- **"~$3 billion equivalent" is itself approximate and multi-currency.** The report says "equivalent," implying the facilities were not necessarily all dollar-denominated — Reliance's exposure tables show borrowings in USD, EUR and JPY (₹1,26,341 crore USD, ₹11,426 crore EUR and ₹18,414 crore JPY as at 31st March, 2025) [RELIANCE-FY25#0715]. A dollar conversion of a partly euro/yen facility is therefore indicative only.

I could not verify the currency composition, tenor, pricing or lender syndicate of the term loan facilities — the report gives only the headline size and purpose in the passage above. The borrowings notes disclose aggregate figures rather than facility-level detail: unsecured term loans from banks of ₹1,56,314 crore non-current and ₹24,226 crore current, with interest rates on unsecured term loans in the range of 0.29% to 10.48% per annum [RELIANCE-FY25#0936], which cannot be tied specifically to the syndicated facilities.
